info.desc: Tommy is the fourth album by the English rock band The Who, released by Track and Polydor in the United Kingdom and Decca and MCA in the United States. A double album telling a loose story about a "deaf, dumb, and blind boy" who becomes the leader of a messianic movement, Tommy was the first musical work to be billed overtly as a rock opera. Released in 1969, the album was mostly composed by guitarist Pete Townshend. In 1998 it was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame for "historical, artistic and significant" value. podcast.body: Released in May 1969, this double album was two years in the making and revolves around the character Tommy Walker. *Rolling Stone*'s 1969 review summarized its plot: Tommy becomes blind, deaf, and dumb after witnessing a murder, eventually becoming a pinball champion, reaching a state of grace, regaining his senses, starting a religion, and finally being discarded by his disciples and returning to isolation. Roger Daltrey later reflected that the album served as a "spiritual awakening" for American youth grappling with the Vietnam War and conscription, deeply capturing people's imaginations. "The opera is, apart from being some of the best rock yet, a statement of Townsend's philosophy. It's about life, he says."

This "great album" was released in the late 1960s and, according to acoustic comparisons, sounded similar to other bands of the era, implying it also maintained the acute guitar characteristics that persisted until Led Zeppelin's breakthrough.
